newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Swedish Riksbank not seen cutting rates soon.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swedish Riksbank not seen cutting rates soon.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, lowered its inflation forecasts for 1997 and 1998 on Thursday but analysts say the weak crown is likely to hamper the bank in cutting interest rates further in the near tem.
The Swedish currency has weakened about six percent against the mark since last October and has been running at a year low against the German currency for the past few days.

"The Riksbank is a lot more positive about the future outlook for inflation," James McKay, economist at PaineWebber told Reuters. "But there will be no further lowering of the repo rate until the crown recovers."

Presenting its latest quarterly inflation report, the Riksbank cut its forecast for the Consumer Price Index to 0.5 percent this year and below two percent in 1998, from 1.5 percent and two percent respectively in a December report.

The Riksbank said the estimates were part of the bank's main scenario and based on unchanged key rates and a somewhat stronger crown than the nominal level 119 on the trade currency weighted (TCW) index.
The Riksbank said it still sees the appropriate level for the crown at a nominal 110-119, corresponding to a real terms level of 109-118.
"The longterm interval remains totally (valid)," Claes Berg, head of the bank's economic unit, told a news conference.
But he said it was more appropriate for the crown to be at the lower end of this range, 110-115 in the TCW index, or 110-114 in real terms.
The crown is currently trading at a much weaker 123.10, in real terms, on the TCW index and at 4.5560 against the mark.
The Riksbank stressed that it did not have a currency goal.
"The Riksbank could lower the repo rate at the current crown level, as long as other indicators look strong," deputy governor Lars Heikensten told a news conference.
He pointed to inflation expectations and other economic conditions as important indicators. For the past five months falls in the monthly CPI have given an negative annualised inflation rate.
But economists say the crown has always been a key monetary indicator and they think its softening and recent volatility could hamper the Riksbank from cutting rates more now.
"They cannot cut (rates) as long as the TCW index is this high," Knut Hallberg, economist at Swedbank, said.
The Riksbank lowered the repo aggressively last year, cutting it 25 times to a current level of 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent. The Riksbank has not changed the rate this year.
But assuming the crown strengthens, or at least stabilises, many economists see the Riksbank lowering the repo again.
"The most important thing is for the crown to go stronger," Stefan Wictorin, analyst at Merita Bank, told Reuters Financial Television.
"The level is not important, I think the Riksbank wants to see a stronger trend in the crown for a longer period of time."
Bjorn Englund, economist at Unibank Markets, expected the repo to come down further.

"All in all, we believe in further rate cuts, but it won't go below 3.75 percent," he said. "Previously, we saw the repo bottoming at 3.50 percent. We are convinced the next rate move will be in a downward direction."
